title: Relational databases
brief: Understand shared relational facts, questions and guarded changes through one shop purchase. Distinguish schema rules, atomicity, concurrent decisions, query work and durability, judge relational fit and choose a practical next route.
ownership_note: Introduce enough of each concern to choose a route; children own detailed design, formal analysis and working procedures.

title: Relational data modelling
brief: Design rows, keys and relationships that express the shop’s facts accurately. Diagnose dependencies and redundancy, distinguish historical facts from derived copies, and judge normalisation and modelling variations through required changes.

neighbouring_ownership.normalisation: Owns precise formal definitions, closure and decomposition methods.
neighbouring_ownership.hierarchies: Owns hierarchy representation comparisons and working maintenance procedures.
neighbouring_ownership.constraints: Owns enforcement, including subtype completeness and tenant references.
neighbouring_ownership.history: Owns temporal procedures; modelling establishes the difference between current and agreed price.

title: Values, missing data and equality
brief: Choose money, time, text and identity representations from their meanings. Reason about conversion, precision, collation, equality, ordering and NULL, including three-valued predicates and uniqueness edge cases.

neighbouring_ownership.query-results: Owns missing matches and the result grain.
neighbouring_ownership.data-modelling: Owns what a row asserts; values owns when an attribute is decomposed or represented as a structured value.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-json: Owns native JSONB operators, validation and indexing.

title: Constraints and data integrity
brief: Express identity, required values, row checks, references and exclusions in enforceable schema rules. Preserve tenant integrity with composite identities and references, and distinguish declarative enforcement, triggers and invariants needing a concurrency protocol.

neighbouring_ownership.access-control: Owns who may read or change rows.
neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns concurrent protocols for rules beyond declarative constraints.
neighbouring_ownership.history: Owns correction and deletion policy; constraints applies that policy to references.

title: Joins and the meaning of a result row
brief: Build SELECT and JOIN results with deliberate row meaning. Predict multiplicity and missing matches, use existence tests, distinguish compatible-row set operations and their duplicates from joining columns, and complete the still-due report by summarising lines and payments separately per order.

neighbouring_ownership.aggregation: Owns general grouping, HAVING, FILTER, empty/count distinctions and windows; query results owns only the narrow per-order GROUP BY/SUM summary required for its report.
neighbouring_ownership.query-execution: Owns physical join methods and execution order.

ownership_note: Own compact UNION ALL/UNION duplicate semantics and orientation to INTERSECT/EXCEPT; no separate thin child.

title: Updates, upserts and bulk imports
brief: Make changes conditional and interpret affected rows. Choose conflict meaning for an upsert and stage, validate and reconcile replayable batches, including a rejected row and a partially processed import.

neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns one-row and multi-row concurrent invariant protocols.
neighbouring_ownership.retry-outcomes: Owns one logical request across unknown commit outcomes.
neighbouring_ownership.schema-change: Owns backfill convergence while callers keep writing.
neighbouring_ownership.application-sql: Owns connection, parameter and failure plumbing.

title: SQL at the application boundary
brief: Preserve query meaning and transaction ownership across drivers, pools and ORMs. Separate parameters from SQL structure, map results, bound repeated queries, and handle one request’s connection, error and cancellation coherently.

neighbouring_ownership.capacity: Owns pool sizing, admission and overload.
neighbouring_ownership.outboxes-jobs: Owns durable external intentions and worker recovery.
neighbouring_ownership.access-control: Owns authority of application and administrative identities.

title: Transactions and isolation
brief: Choose atomic work and isolation from the invariant being preserved. Distinguish committed visibility, statement and transaction snapshots and serial outcomes; develop sound one-row stock and multi-row capacity protocols.

neighbouring_ownership.locks: Owns explicit lock scope, ordering and wait diagnosis.
neighbouring_ownership.storage-durability: Owns how versions and logs implement physical history, without treating storage versions as business history.

title: Query execution and performance
brief: Follow rows through scans, joins, grouping and sorting. Use measured plans to locate bad cardinality estimates, repeated work, spills and data movement; test a repair against realistic parameters and workload.

neighbouring_ownership.indexes: Owns access-path design, not all query repair.
neighbouring_ownership.incidents: Owns separating execution work from admission and lock waits.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-plans: Owns native PostgreSQL counters and plan behaviour.

title: Storage and durability
brief: Connect logical updates to pages, buffers, retained row versions and cleanup, distinguishing reusable space, file shrinkage and write amplification. Explain write-ahead ordering, commit durability and restart recovery, and separate them from recovery after lost storage or an unwanted committed change.

neighbouring_ownership.backups: Owns restorable history and recovery reconciliation.
neighbouring_ownership.replicas: Owns copied history, progress and read routing.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-vacuum: Owns native retention diagnosis and transaction age.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-wal: Owns native settings and crash drills.

title: Diagnosing a database incident
brief: Start with a slow or failing request and use evidence to distinguish pool delay, lock waits, expensive execution and storage pressure. Choose a bounded intervention and account for its recovery cost.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-operations: Owns PostgreSQL evidence and native intervention.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-operations: Owns native cluster health and secure operation.

title: Sharding and distributed SQL
brief: Choose a distribution boundary from local work, invariant scope and the actual bottleneck. Distinguish replicas from shards, explain authoritative replicated history, acknowledgements and quorum availability, and separate agreement within one partition from atomic commit across partitions. Derive locality, skew, fan-out and coordination from the key.

neighbouring_ownership.placement: Owns latency and survival across failure domains.
neighbouring_ownership.replicas: Owns copied-history progress and read routing; distribution establishes quorum-based agreement within one replicated partition.

title: Inside PostgreSQL
brief: Trace one connection and request through PostgreSQL processes, shared buffers, heap tuples and indexes. Explain tuple visibility, HOT updates and their physical limits so native plans and maintenance have a concrete physical setting.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-vacuum: Owns retained horizons and transaction-age maintenance.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-wal: Owns durability controls and crash drills.

title: Inside CockroachDB
brief: Trace SQL data through ordered keys, ranges, local storage and replicated ownership. Explain splits, leases and replica agreement with enough detail to see why a hotspot can persist as a cluster grows.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-transactions: Owns native intents and commit/retry paths.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-performance: Owns SQL/KV/network work and hot-range diagnosis.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-operations: Owns health, identity and removal procedures.
neighbouring_ownership.distribution: Owns transferable replica-agreement concepts; this article develops their native range, Raft and lease application.
